title: I built a browser based Mordhau style melee combat game with ai, thoughts?
author: No-Difference629

comments.author: Shaz_berries
comments.body: How did you leverage AI to create this?

replies.author: No-Difference629
replies.body:
For me it was way more about workflow than just “using AI.”

I started with a tiny barebones mechanic that felt fun on its own, then iterated carefully from there. Small changes, frequent commits, lots of backups before risky shifts.

I also try to build everything modular from the start so it’s expandable later and doesn’t turn into a brick wall when you want to add features. That part matters more than people think.

AI speeds things up immensely, but it isn’t completely magic. You still have to plan systems in your head, think through edge cases, and structure things like a programmer. When it spits out something wrong (which it does occasionally of course), you still have to debug, research, and fix it yourself.

The real leverage came from tightening the loop between idea → implement → test → refine, over and over until it started taking shape.

replies.author: Shaz_berries
replies.body: Sounds reasonable! I'm using a similar flow to create my 2d game engine in TypeScript. Glad to hear it's working for you as well! I would've been skeptical if you said it's a silver bullet :)

replies.body: That’s cool! I’d love to check out what you’re working on.

comments.author: erofamiliar
comments.body:
wtf, that looks great

Also, from your other post:

>*UV blood maps that dynamically paint wounds onto the mesh and drip similar to how the game "Overgrowth" handles slash marks*

thank goodness someone's doing it because I love that effect, lol. I'm sure other games have done it but I can really only think of Overgrowth, and that one mod for Blade and Sorcery

replies.author: No-Difference629
replies.body:
Thank you! I really appreciate that.
I was always mesmerized by the effect in overgrowth and could only relive that in blade & sorcery as well haha. I’ve always thought melee games feel way more satisfying when you can see the consequences of every hit instead of just watching a health bar drop or generic blood effects. 
Glad someone noticed that detail.

I used Gemini in AI Studio to scaffold the initial foundation, then iterated heavily with Codex. I also experimented with Cursor for a few refactors.
